reason: Conversation 1 wasted turns on irrelevant checks for a totally dead machine (door seal and spray arms, then child lock and delay start despite 'no display at all'), never actually proposed the simple spur-fuse swap, and instead pushed the homeowner toward opening the spur wiring terminals before ending with unsupported named causes (main control PCB, door hinge loom). Conversation 2, though verbose and with some US-isms in the opener, quickly pivoted to correct UK fused-spur advice with the switch off, worked within the homeowner's stated limits (checking for a plug under the sink without pulling the unit out, a power-off reset, holding the door-top on/off button), and escalated appropriately with warranty, Neff service and a useful summary for the engineer. Its claim that a lit neon means the spur fuse is fine is plausible but not universal and slightly closed off the fuse-swap route, and its 'common causes' were hedged rather than asserted, so it still clearly served the homeowner better.
